messages.subject: Testlet model M2 and RMSEA
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. Chalmers and community,

I am trying to run a graded response testlet model or second order model with the the"mirt" function and "MHRM" specifically.

When doing so, I get an error message regarding the computation of M2 and the associated RMSEA that I want to get :

> M2_mod.md.bifactorGR<-M2(mod.md.bifactorGR, QMC=TRUE)
Error in rowSums(delta[, constrain[[i]]])

Could you please please help me in how to get M2 and associated RMSEA for this model ?

Could you also please tell me if my syntax is right regarding the model I want to run (testlet GRM)  with the the"mirt" function and "MHRM" specifically ?

I am sorry to ask these simple questions but I am a beginner with IRT and MIRT package.

Many thanks in advance.

Peter

Below the syntax :

library(mirt)
cp<-read.csv("cp.csv", sep=";")

# Testlet GR Model)
spec<-'G = 1-16
S1 = 1-3
S2 = 3-6
S3 = 6-9
S4 = 9-12
S5 = 12-16

CONSTRAIN = (1, a1,a2), (2, a1,a2), (3, a1,a2)

CONSTRAIN = (4,a1,a3), (5,a1,a3), (6,a1,a3)

CONSTRAIN = (7,a1,a4), (8,a1,a4), (9,a1,a4)

CONSTRAIN = (8,a1,a5), (9,a1,a5),(10,a1,a5)

CONSTRAIN = (10,a1,a6), (11,a1,a6), (12,a1,a6)

CONSTRAIN = (13,a1,a7),(14, a1,a7), (15,a1,a7), (16,a1,a7)

FREE = (GROUP, COV_22),(GROUP, COV_33),(GROUP, COV_44),(GROUP, COV_55),
(GROUP, COV_66)'

mod.md.bifactorGR<-mirt(cp,model=spec, itemtype='graded', SE=T, method='MHRM')
mod.md.bifactorGR

coef(mod.md.bifactorGR)

LD_mod.md.bifactorGR<-residuals(mod.md.bifactorGR, type="LD")
LD_mod.md.bifactorGR

Itemfit_mod.md.bifactorGR<-itemfit(mod.md.bifactorGR, QMC=TRUE)
Itemfit_mod.md.bifactorGR

M2_mod.md.bifactorGR<-M2(mod.md.bifactorGR, QMC=TRUE)
M2_mod.md.bifactorGR

messages.subject_clean: Estimating multidimensional a priori item parameters
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am on a journey learning MIRT as a complete beginner and have a better grasp on it after reading Reckase's textbook on the matter.

However, I still have one major gap in my knowledge: where do the initial item parameters come from? I can find information regarding estimating item parameters for known thetas and estimating thetas with known item parameters, but this seems like a paradox.

How can I know the thetas of a group of examinees without first knowing the item parameters?

Let's assume I have already observed the traditional test results of 100 examinees for 20 questions each and want to construct a mirt model. How do I pick the parameters? An example shown on the mirtCAT github page is:

library("mirtCAT")
set.seed(1)

# multidimensional IRT model with simple structure (continuation from Example 2)
nitems <- 100
a <- rlnorm(nitems, .2, .3) # from Example 2
d <- runif(nitems, -3, 3)
g <- rep(0.2, nitems)

a <- matrix(c(a, numeric(nitems*2), rlnorm(nitems, .2, .3)), 200)
d <- c(d, runif(nitems, -3, 3))
g <- c(g, rep(0.2, nitems))

pars <- data.frame(a1 = a[,1], a2=a[,2], d = d, g = g)
head(pars)
pars[98:103, ]
tail(pars)

# correlation between traits
lc <- matrix(c(1,.6,.6,1), 2, 2)

mirt_object <- generate.mirt_object(pars, itemtype = "3PL",
                                    latent_covariance = lc)

It seems the item parameters are arbitrarily decided from distributions.

If anyone could explain what I am missing or point me toward a related thread that would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks all,
Peter

messages.subject: Estimating Person Fit On The Fly
messages.subject_clean: Estimating Person Fit On The Fly
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Is it possible to estimate person infit/outfit or Zh value using just one participant's response pattern given the items' psychometric properties? If not, is there an established method to evaluate person fit on-the-fly in an adaptive environment?

The goal is to be able to calculate interim person index as one would calculate interim theta in a CAT environment. This will allow us to stop the CAT if we suspect someone is not doing the test properly.

For example,

require(mirt)
data(Science, package = 'mirt')
mod <- mirt(Science, 1)
all_Theta=fscores(mod, method='MAP')
mirt::personfit(mod, Theta=all_Theta) # This works

# Try to calculate the person fit for a specific person.
person_Theta=fscores(mod, method='MAP', response.pattern = c(1,2,3,4))
mirt::personfit(mod, Theta=person_Theta[1]) # This doesn't work

Thank you!
Aiden

Hello,

First of all, thank you so much for setting up this forum. I am looking for help regarding item characteristic curves for dichotomous items. The data frame includes some dichotomous and some polytomous items. I have fit a partial credit model using the command below:

model <- mirt(data = data, model = 1, itemtype = "Rasch")

I am creating item characteristic curves using the command below:

plot(x = model, type = "trace")

However, this only creates one curve for the dichotomous items. For example, the plot below. I have tried coding my data as 0-1, or 1-2. The result is the same.

I do see three separate curves for the polytomous items, but only one for the dichotomous ones. Is there a way to create two separate curves for the dichotomous items as well? I read on another thread on the group <https://groups.google.com/g/mirt-package/c/sLllMLAll9c/m/K80TJ33iAwAJ> that there is no easy way to find the value of intersection, but wasn't sure if there is still a way to at least plot it. I would appreciate any suggestions. Thank you in advance

messages.subject_clean: Item Characteristic Curve for dichotomous items
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sayali,

In the documentation of plot you'll see a 'drop2' argument which indicates whether the first category of a dichotomous response model should be dropped since it's easily identifiable (just 1 - p(theta) for all theta). If you want to change the TRUE default just pass FALSE, like the following:

library(mirt)
mod <- mirt(expand.table(LSAT7), 1)
plot(mod, type='trace', drop2=FALSE)
plot(mod, type='trace', drop2=FALSE, which.item=1)

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Estimating multidimensional a priori item parameters
messages.subject_clean: Estimating multidimensional a priori item parameters
messages.body_plain:
Hi Peter,

I am a beginner myself but I will try to answer, in case you have not found an answer already.

Item parameters come from the mirt package, which creates a mirt-type object based on data and some further options passed through the function. In the example that you have presented here the item parameters are indeed randomly generated, but I believe the purpose for this is to demonstrate the use of generate.mirt_object() function, which requires item parameters that are already known.

I think the confusion comes from the fact that item parameters are not calculated in this example. Traditionally, in item response theory the item parameters are calculated on a data sample. The Wikipedia page for IRT has a lot of good information and the 3 parameter logistic model, for example, calculates 3 item parameters based on the probability of answering a specific question correctly. I believe the theta in that equation is the "true" ability given at the conclusion of the test. Item parameters are measured on specific populations (usually people who take the tests) and you basically just fit a logistic function over the probability of answering each item correctly (it might not be a logistic function, there are other models as well, but that one seems to be the most popular one). My understanding of IRT is that it measures the ability of the sample and then compares that ability to the following test takers, therefore updating of parameters is important feature of CATs in general that should happen every so often to make sure that the measurement are correct or as close as possible to correct. I see it as a tool to compare one to the general population (of test takers), which is why CATs usually give their results in percentiles rather than absolute marks. Once the mathematical function of choice is fitted to the data (using mirt package), you have calculated item parameters and using those you can then generate CATs (using the mirtCAT library).

I found it helpful to think about 1PL models first, where only the difficulty of an item is taken into account and then add the discrimination parameter and so on...

Hope this helps

Best wishes,
Siyan

>

> nitems <- 100
> a <- rlnorm(nitems, .2, .3) # from Example 2
> d <- runif(nitems, -3, 3)
> g <- rep(0.2, nitems)
>
> a <- matrix(c(a, numeric(nitems*2), rlnorm(nitems, .2, .3)), 200)
> d <- c(d, runif(nitems, -3, 3))
> g <- c(g, rep(0.2, nitems))
>
> pars <- data.frame(a1 = a[,1], a2=a[,2], d = d, g = g)
> head(pars)
> pars[98:103, ]
> tail(pars)
>
> # correlation between traits
> lc <- matrix(c(1,.6,.6,1), 2, 2)
>
> mirt_object <- generate.mirt_object(pars, itemtype = "3PL",
>                                     latent_covariance = lc)
>
>
> It seems the item parameters are arbitrarily decided from distributions.
>
> If anyone could explain what I am missing or point me toward a related thread that would be greatly appreciated.
>
> Thanks all,
> Peter

messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil,

I'm currently trying to fit a mirt model with predefined parameters in a MCAT-simulation with real data. When doing that for unidimensional models (one dimension at a time) everything works fine, but with my multidimensional model I get an error message I can't seem to solve. Could that one a bug or am I doing something wrong? Could you help me?

Background:
I calibrated a mirt-model for my MCAT simulation with some real personality data (6-point Likert-scale, model = "graded"). In the next step I want to simulate a MCAT with a different (also real) dataset in order to observe whether my calibrated MCAT works as expected with independent data. My calibration data was N > 20k and my confirmation dataset is N > 20k as well, without any missing values in either of it. My mirt model has 14 dimensions and includes all covariances (between-item multidimensionality).

Here's my code:

load(file = calibration mirt-model)

coef <- coef(mirt.model)

model <- 'F1 = i7,i22,i37,i53,i69,i85,i100,i115,i130,i144,i159,i172,i196,i204
          F2 = i8,i23,i38,i54,i70,i86,i101,i116,i131,i145,i173,i186
          F3 = i9,i24,i39,i55,i71,i87,i102,i117,i132,i146,i160,i174,i187,i197,i205

          F7 = i14,i29,i44,i60,i76,i92,i107,i122,i151,i165,i179,i191
          F8 = i2,i16,i31,i46,i62,i78,i94,i109,i124,i138,i153,i167,i181,i192,i201,i208
          F9 = i1,i15,i30,i45,i61,i77,i93,i108,i123,i137,i152,i166,i180,i200,i207
          F10 = i3,i17,i32,i47,i63,i79,i95,i110,i125,i139,i154,i168,i182
          F11 = i10,i25,i40,i56,i72,i88,i103,i118,i133,i147,i161,i175
          F12 = i4,i18,i33,i48,i64,i80,i96,i111,i126,i140,i155,i169,i183,i193,i202,i209
          F13 = i5,i19,i34,i49,i65,i81,i97,i112,i127,i141,i156,i170,i184
          F14 = i6,i20,i35,i50,i66,i82,i98,i113,i128,i142,i157,i171,i185,i194,i203,i210
          COV = F1*F2*F3*F4*F5*F6*F7*F8*F9*F10*F11*F12*F13*F14'

pars <- mirt(data = data, model = model, 'graded', SE = TRUE, pars = "values")

pars$est <- FALSE

# overwriting the pars object with the precalibrated parameters of the first mirt-model
for (item in items) { # items is a vector of all items used in the model
   pars$value[which(pars$item == item)] <- coef[[item]][1,]
}

pars$value[which(pars$item == "GROUP")] <- coef$GroupPars[1,]

#using the pars object to fit a mirt model with "old" parameters on "new" data
mirt.model.confirmation <- mirt(data = data, model = model, itemtype = 'graded', pars = pars, method = "MHRM")

That always throws me this error message:

error in colMeans(do.call(rbind, aveAR)) :
  'x' must be an array of at least two dimensions

(translated error message from german)

Do you have any clue? It's very important for my doctoral thesis to solve this, so I would be very thankful for your help!

Best wishes

Nick
